import Mathlib

-- Precondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def mergeSort_precond (v : List Int) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start precond
  True
  -- !benchmark @end precond

-- !benchmark @start auxcode
/-- Merge two lists, assumed sorted, into one sorted list. -/
def mergeAux : List Int → List Int → List Int
  | [], l2 => l2
  | a :: as, [] => a :: as
  | a :: as, b :: bs =>
      if a ≤ b then a :: mergeAux as (b :: bs) else b :: mergeAux (a :: as) bs
termination_by l1 l2 => l1.length + l2.length

/-- Recursive divide-and-conquer merge sort. -/
def msort : List Int → List Int
  | [] => []
  | [a] => [a]
  | a :: b :: rest =>
      mergeAux (msort ((a :: b :: rest).take ((rest.length + 2) / 2)))
               (msort ((a :: b :: rest).drop ((rest.length + 2) / 2)))
termination_by l => l.length
decreasing_by
  · simp only [List.length_take, List.length_cons]
    omega
  · simp only [List.length_drop, List.length_cons]
    omega
-- !benchmark @end auxcode

-- Main function definitions
def mergeSort (v : List Int) (h_precond : mergeSort_precond v) : List Int :=
  -- !benchmark @start code
  msort v
  -- !benchmark @end code

-- Postcondition definitions
@[reducible, simp]
def mergeSort_postcond (v : List Int) (result : List Int) (h_precond : mergeSort_precond v) : Prop :=
  -- !benchmark @start postcond
   List.Sorted (· ≤ ·) result ∧ result.Perm v
  -- !benchmark @end postcond

-- !benchmark @start lemma
theorem mergeAux_perm : ∀ l1 l2 : List Int, (mergeAux l1 l2).Perm (l1 ++ l2) := by
  intro l1 l2
  induction l1, l2 using mergeAux.induct with
  | case1 l2 => simp [mergeAux]
  | case2 a as => simp [mergeAux]
  | case3 a as b bs hle ih =>
      simp only [mergeAux, if_pos hle, List.cons_append]
      exact ih.cons a
  | case4 a as b bs hgt ih =>
      simp only [mergeAux, if_neg hgt]
      exact (ih.cons b).trans List.perm_middle.symm

theorem mergeAux_sorted : ∀ l1 l2 : List Int, l1.Sorted (· ≤ ·) → l2.Sorted (· ≤ ·) →
    (mergeAux l1 l2).Sorted (· ≤ ·) := by
  intro l1 l2
  induction l1, l2 using mergeAux.induct with
  | case1 l2 => intro _ h2; simpa [mergeAux] using h2
  | case2 a as => intro h1 _; simpa [mergeAux] using h1
  | case3 a as b bs hle ih =>
      intro h1 h2
      simp only [mergeAux, if_pos hle]
      rw [List.sorted_cons] at h1 ⊢
      refine ⟨?_, ih h1.2 h2⟩
      intro x hx
      have hx' := (mergeAux_perm as (b :: bs)).mem_iff.mp hx
      simp only [List.mem_append, List.mem_cons] at hx'
      rcases hx' with h | h | h
      · exact h1.1 x h
      · exact h ▸ hle
      · exact le_trans hle ((List.sorted_cons.mp h2).1 x h)
  | case4 a as b bs hgt ih =>
      intro h1 h2
      simp only [mergeAux, if_neg hgt]
      have hba : b ≤ a := le_of_lt (lt_of_not_le hgt)
      rw [List.sorted_cons] at h2 ⊢
      refine ⟨?_, ih h1 h2.2⟩
      intro x hx
      have hx' := (mergeAux_perm (a :: as) bs).mem_iff.mp hx
      simp only [List.mem_append, List.mem_cons] at hx'
      rcases hx' with (h | h) | h
      · exact h ▸ hba
      · exact le_trans hba ((List.sorted_cons.mp h1).1 x h)
      · exact h2.1 x h

theorem msort_perm : ∀ l : List Int, (msort l).Perm l := by
  intro l
  induction l using msort.induct with
  | case1 => simp [msort]
  | case2 a => simp [msort]
  | case3 a b rest ih1 ih2 =>
      rw [msort]
      refine (mergeAux_perm _ _).trans ?_
      refine ((ih1.append ih2).trans ?_)
      rw [List.take_append_drop]

theorem msort_sorted : ∀ l : List Int, (msort l).Sorted (· ≤ ·) := by
  intro l
  induction l using msort.induct with
  | case1 => simp [msort]
  | case2 a => simp [msort]
  | case3 a b rest ih1 ih2 =>
      rw [msort]
      exact mergeAux_sorted _ _ ih1 ih2
-- !benchmark @end lemma

-- Proof content
theorem mergeSort_postcond_satisfied (v : List Int) (h_precond : mergeSort_precond v) :
    mergeSort_postcond v (mergeSort v h_precond) h_precond := by
  -- !benchmark @start proof
  exact ⟨msort_sorted v, msort_perm v⟩
  -- !benchmark @end proof

**What I did**, all inside the marker regions:

- **auxcode** (`Solution.lean:12-30`): `mergeAux`, a two-list merge with `termination_by l1.length + l2.length`, and `msort`, the divide-and-conquer sort splitting `a :: b :: rest` at `(rest.length + 2) / 2` via `take`/`drop`, with `decreasing_by` goals closed by `simp [length_take/length_drop]` + `omega`.
- **code**: `mergeSort v _ := msort v`.
- **lemma**: four results, each by functional induction (`mergeAux.induct` / `msort.induct`):
  - `mergeAux_perm`: `mergeAux l1 l2 ~ l1 ++ l2` (the `b`-branch uses `List.perm_middle`).
  - `mergeAux_sorted`: merging two sorted lists is sorted; the head-bound obligation is discharged by transporting membership through `mergeAux_perm`.
  - `msort_perm`: composes the two recursive perms with `List.take_append_drop`.
  - `msort_sorted`.
- **proof**: `exact ⟨msort_sorted v, msort_perm v⟩`.

No `sorry`/`partial`/axioms, and no files other than `Solution.lean` were touched.
